prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1481; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red light on eastbound Highway 6 in Sugar Land, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by a sedan operated by Driver 2. Driver 1 was the only occupant of the front seat, with a Passenger seated in the rear, and both were identified at the scene. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was evaluated by responding medical personnel, though it is not yet clear whether the reported injury resulted from this collision or from another cause. Driver 2 stated that the vehicle did not stop in time, and this account is consistent with the statements of two independent witnesses who were present at the intersection and with photographs taken at the scene. The rear bumper and trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle show damage that matches the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle was observed or reported. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Officers noted no signs of impairment and issued a citation to Driver 2 for failure to control speed. Follow-up with medical providers is recommended to determine the source of the reported symptoms.
